long_biography.plain_text:
Michael Steven Ovitz began in the William Morris Agency mailroom and rose to become a television agent. In 1975, he and four colleagues founded Creative Artists Agency. As chairman, he helped turn CAA into a leading Hollywood talent agency. Its packages of writers, directors and actors, coupled with representation coordinated across the firm, strengthened talent's position with studios.

Ovitz left CAA to serve as president of The Walt Disney Company. He later founded talent-management and production businesses, then concentrated increasingly on technology and media investment. Today he chairs Gallery Ventures, a venture-capital firm, and has advised companies and investment firms including Palantir Technologies and Andreessen Horowitz. His art activity remains distinct from the fortune-building story: he is a collector and serves as a Museum of Modern Art trustee.
